neighbours.label: The give/provide benefaction frame at the slot after the recipient where the benefit is named (gives the rider excellent grip, provides the house with insulation)
fire: The raised deck gives the house a clear view over the bay.
Soft bristles provide the gums with gentle but thorough cleaning.
A wide stance gives the climber better balance on the ledge.
The new bypass provides commuters with a faster route into town.
Double glazing gives the bedroom excellent protection from street noise.
The loan scheme provides young growers with the capital to buy land.
Padded straps give the hiker extra comfort on long descents.
The museum provides visitors with free audio guides in six languages.
quiet: The house with the raised deck overlooks the bay.
Gums with soft tissue bleed more easily during cleaning.
The climber with the widest stance reached the ledge first.
Commuters took the new bypass into town this morning.
The bedroom with double glazing faces the street.
Young growers borrowed the capital to buy land from the scheme.
The hiker with padded straps descended slowly.
Visitors collected free audio guides at the museum entrance.

predictions: Sentences of the form 'X gives Y [benefit]' or 'X provides Y with [benefit]' reach 0.17-0.5, peaking on ' with' or the first word of the benefit. Twins with comitative 'with', receive/take/borrow from the recipient's side, or 'give up' stay under 0.03.
notes: Probe: 'give the rider excellent grip' 0.508 (peak ' excellent'), 'provide the house with insulation' 0.504 (peak ' with'), 'provides small farmers with access' 0.302, 'gives you the energy' 0.222 (peak ' you'), 'provided the school with new' 0.173; 'The rider with the widest tyres' 0.005, 'received ... from' 0.013, 'took out loans' 0.006, 'gave up' 0.020, floor 0.007. Card peaks ' with' x13, ' give' x4, ' gives' x4, ' a' x3, ' you' x2, ' providing', 提供; the + pole's output suppresses access/insight/benefit/opportunities, so this pole predicts the benefit noun.
